rationale: Zambia successfully completed its IMF Extended Credit Facility (ECF) programme in November 2023 and finalised Eurobond restructuring under the G20 Common Framework in October 2023 (USD 6.3B in external commercial debt restructured). The sovereign was upgraded from SD/CC to B- by S&P and Fitch in Q1 2024. Positive factors include: IMF programme completion, improved fiscal consolidation (fiscal deficit reduced to 7.6% of GDP in 2023), debt relief terms providing short-term breathing room, and resumption of market access. Key risks: high public debt (105% of GDP), reliance on copper revenues, climate vulnerability of energy sector (hydropower), and continued need for concessional financing. Copper price recovery and ZCCM-IH dividend income support fiscal position.
creditHistory: Completed debt restructuring in 2023. Previously in arrears on Eurobond payments from 2020–2023 following COVID-19 economic shock and copper price decline.

rationale: ZESCO faces severe liquidity pressure driven by three compounding factors: (1) electricity tariffs set below cost-recovery levels by ZESCO's regulator (ERB), resulting in a structural operating deficit; (2) drought-related reservoir depletion at Kariba Dam reducing hydropower generation capacity by approximately 40% in 2024–25, forcing expensive diesel generation supplementation; (3) significant receivables from government entities and high-density residential areas that remain uncollected. The company has 62-day overdue semi-annual interest on the AfDB Power System Modernisation loan. Sovereign guarantee from Ministry of Finance provides an ultimate backstop but does not resolve ZESCO's operational cash flow position. Tariff reform is a critical reform trigger. Watch listed by AfDB Zambia Country Office.

RDA has no independent revenue stream; it is wholly dependent on GRZ budget transfers from the Road Fund (fuel levies) and Treasury allocations. Its credit quality is therefore a notch below the sovereign, reflecting execution risk and the additional layer of budget release dependency. RDA's standalone creditworthiness is constrained by procurement capacity limitations, a history of delayed contractor payments, and a current procurement irregularity investigation (suspected bid-rigging) flagged by AfDB. All AfDB Lusaka-Ndola loan obligations are fully sovereign-guaranteed; repayment risk remains with the Republic of Zambia rated B-.
budgetTransferReliability: Moderate — subject to GRZ fiscal constraints

rationale: LWSC serves approximately 2.2 million people in Lusaka with water and sewerage services. Tariff levels are regulated by NWASCO and have historically been set below cost recovery. A tariff adjustment of 23% was approved in 2024 improving the financial position. LWSC benefits from sovereign guarantee on all AfDB loans; standalone creditworthiness reflects persistent operational cash deficits, aging infrastructure (30–50% of distribution network exceeds design life), and collection rate of 68%. Positive factors: improving billing systems post-AfDB WASH project, recent leadership changes introducing commercial management discipline, and World Bank parallel support for institutional strengthening.

ZAFC operates as an on-lending vehicle channelling concessional AfDB funds to smallholder cooperatives. It carries sovereign backing from the Ministry of Finance, providing a critical credit enhancement. Standalone ZAFC creditworthiness is constrained by agricultural weather risk (drought/flood cycles), thin capitalisation (CAR of 14.2%), and NPL ratio of 18.7% in its legacy portfolio. The AfDB Agriculture Transformation Programme has introduced enhanced credit appraisal standards and crop insurance requirements for sub-borrowers. Collection performance on AfDB-funded tranches is better than the legacy portfolio. Rated at par with sovereign (B-) given full government ownership and strategic importance.

IDC Zambia is a non-sovereign borrower (no GRZ guarantee on the AfDB private sector loan). The corporation holds equity stakes in 35 companies across mining, agriculture, tourism, and manufacturing. IDC generates income primarily through dividends and management fees. The Lusaka-Kafue Industrial Zone project is performing well with 38 of 50 factory shells occupied and generating rental income. Debt service coverage ratio of 1.42x is adequate. IDC's consolidated balance sheet has improved following ZCCM-IH dividend recovery and sale of non-core assets. Principal risk remains concentration in cyclical copper mining sector exposures and limited track record as a debt issuer without sovereign backing.

riskCategory: Moderate Risk — Sovereign Ministry (Above Sovereign Floor)
rationale: The Ministry of Agriculture acts as co-implementing agency with ZAFC on the Agriculture Transformation Programme but does not hold any direct loan obligations to AfDB. Its credit assessment relates to fiduciary and institutional capacity risk for project implementation purposes. Assessment considers: adequacy of ministry procurement systems (PEFA B rating), track record of budget execution, staff capacity for project management, and food security policy stability. Rated one notch above sovereign (B vs B-) reflecting strong institutional standing, Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP) operational continuity, and consistent budget support from both donors and GRZ.
foodSecurityStatus: Moderate food insecurity (southern and western provinces drought-affected)

rationale: Bank of Zambia is a recipient of AfDB Technical Assistance and capacity-building grants, not a loan borrower. Credit assessment relates to institutional capacity for absorbing TA effectively and fiduciary management of TA grant funds. BoZ has demonstrated improving monetary policy credibility through successful inflation targeting (policy rate 13.5% in 2025) and improved foreign exchange reserve management. Foreign reserves stand at 3.2 months of import cover. BoZ's financial position closely mirrors the sovereign; independence from GRZ interference is constitutionally enshrined but constrained in practice. Assessment capped at sovereign rating (B-) for risk classification purposes.

riskCategory: Moderate Risk — Revenue Agency (Above Sovereign Floor)
rationale: ZRA is a non-borrowing beneficiary of technical assistance under the PFM Reform Support Programme II. Its rating reflects institutional capacity, TA absorption effectiveness, and fiduciary management of project resources. ZRA has demonstrated strong performance: tax-to-GDP ratio improved from 14.2% to 17.8% between 2020 and 2024, ASYCUDA World customs platform successfully deployed at all major border posts, and GFS-compliant revenue reporting adopted. AfDB TA focus areas — e-filing expansion, transfer pricing enforcement, and excise modernisation — are progressing on schedule. One notch above sovereign reflecting ZRA's strong institutional capacity and improving revenue mobilisation trajectory.

riskCategory: Moderate Risk — Development NGO with Strong Track Record
rationale: CFU Zambia is a grant recipient (no repayment obligation) under the AfDB climate-smart agriculture programme. Its internal rating reflects implementation capacity risk, financial management, and programme delivery track record. CFU has 30 years of operational history in Zambia, a strong technical team, and established relationships with 180,000+ smallholder farmers in seven provinces. Financial management assessment: clean audit opinions for 5 consecutive years, robust internal controls, and transparent donor reporting. Key risks: NGO funding dependence, staff turnover in field operations, and weather-related programme disruptions. Rated B (investment-grade equivalent for NGO) reflecting best-practice NGO financial management.
